aspect_adaptations: memory_ownership is read as result-materialization discipline (projection width, SOQL for-loop chunking, heap pressure inside the host Apex transaction); concurrency is read as FOR UPDATE locking semantics, async transaction contexts and Batch Apex QueryLocator scale; error_handling covers query-time exceptions only, since SOQL itself has no DML error surface.

assertions_contracts.best_practice: SOQL has no assertion construct of its own, so a declared contract checked in review and in Apex tests is the correct adaptation; nothing in the platform offers a stronger mechanism the guide omits.
assertions_contracts.evidence: The contract format is this guide's policy, consistent with the Apex Developer Guide's cardinality-sensitive constructs (single-row assignment QueryException) that it cites.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Every query carries a written contract before its text: source object, exact projection, expected cardinality (0, 0..1, 1, bounded n), ordering or an explicit 'unordered', row budget, security mode, and zero-row behavior; an unwritten cardinality is treated as a defect.

bounded_work.best_practice: Each figure spot-checked against Salesforce's published limits: the 50,000-row ceiling, the OFFSET 2,000 maximum (also restated in the current Developer Limits quick reference) and the QueryLocator figures all match.
bounded_work.evidence: Winter '27 changed Apex heap, not any SOQL row or statement limit this table carries.
bounded_work.guide_position: Per-transaction budgets stated with headroom: 100/200 SOQL statements, 50,000 retrieved rows (relationship-subquery child rows count), 10,000 rows via Database.getQueryLocator, 50,000,000 via a Batch Apex QueryLocator, OFFSET capped at 2,000, API query batch at most 2,000 (200 with two or more long-text fields); every production query carries a LIMIT, locator or keyset bound.

concurrency.best_practice: Matches the documented locking and async-limit model; the callout-releases-locks behavior is a real platform rule the guide correctly treats as a design constraint.
concurrency.evidence: No Winter '27 change to FOR UPDATE semantics or async SOQL budgets was found.
concurrency.guide_position: FOR UPDATE locking is explicit (locks held to transaction end, ORDER BY forbidden, locks released if the transaction makes a callout - cited to the release notes); async contexts get 200 statements but the same 50,000-row ceiling; Batch Apex start queries are designed to the QueryLocator's 50M-record span with 200-record default scope.

error_handling.best_practice: Consistent with the Apex Developer Guide's governor and query documentation.
error_handling.evidence: The error model is unchanged in the current release line.
error_handling.guide_position: Governor exhaustion is designed out, not caught (LimitException is uncatchable); empty results and failed queries are distinct outcomes with distinct handling; single-row assignment QueryException is avoided by List-based access; non-selective query errors in trigger context are treated as a selectivity failure, not an exception to absorb.

formatting.best_practice: Accurate about the tooling reality: there is no standalone SOQL formatter or language server; completion lives inside apex_ls. Declaring conventions instead of inventing a tool is the honest posture.
formatting.evidence: Salesforce's own documentation and editor tooling offer no standalone SOQL formatter to pin instead.
formatting.guide_position: Guide conventions only - keywords uppercase, one clause per line, one field per line in long projections, subqueries indented one level, enforced by review; the guide states plainly that no formatter enforces this in the estate.

memory_ownership.best_practice: Matches the platform's documented behavior, including the FIELDS() support table: unbounded FIELDS(ALL)/FIELDS(CUSTOM) are not supported in Apex (inline or dynamic) or Bulk API 2.0, and are supported via CLI/APIs only when rows are limited to at most 200 - exactly the guide's position that they are exploration tools outside Apex.
memory_ownership.evidence: The current SOQL reference's bounded/unbounded support table confirms the guide's FIELDS() rules in substance (Apex: bounded FIELDS(STANDARD) supported, unbounded not supported).
memory_ownership.guide_position: Project exactly the fields the caller reads (touching an unselected field throws at runtime); SOQL for loops stream results in 200-record chunks instead of materializing the full set; aggregates compute in the engine so rows never materialize just to be counted; FIELDS(ALL)/FIELDS(CUSTOM) barred from production projections and stated not to run in Apex.

security.best_practice: This is the current documented posture: at API 67.0+ Apex SOQL/DML default to user mode, and the current security and sharing chapter is version-forked on that line.
security.evidence: Unlike the sibling Apex guide, this guide states the 67.0 fork correctly in both its runtime-assumptions and security sections.
security.guide_position: Bind every value (static :binds; Database.queryWithBinds with an access level for dynamic SOQL); String.escapeSingleQuotes explicitly rejected as a strategy; dynamic identifiers allowlisted from Schema describe metadata; security mode named on every query - WITH USER_MODE default, WITH SYSTEM_MODE only with a written reason; WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED correctly identified as the retired predecessor (API 45.0-66.0); the API 67.0 user-mode/with-sharing default fork is stated in section 2.

static_analysis.best_practice: Matches the real tool surface - Salesforce provides no standalone SOQL analyzer; selectivity is a data-dependent property the Query Plan tool exists to measure.
static_analysis.evidence: The guide's tooling claims were verified against the analyzer's documented engine model.
static_analysis.guide_position: No fictitious SOQL linter is invented: analysis is the Query Plan tool against org-shaped data for selectivity, Code Analyzer PMD rules for queries embedded in Apex, and the Limits class for budget assertions in tests.

testing.best_practice: Consistent with Apex testing best practice (factory data, SeeAllData off, runAs authority tests) applied at query granularity.
testing.evidence: No platform testing change in Winter '27 displaces this split.
testing.guide_position: Half validation / half adversarial against org-shaped fixtures (volume, skew, null density): exact-row and cardinality tests, keyset walks past 2,000 rows returning every row exactly once, Limits snapshots asserting budget headroom, injection strings and identifier attacks as binds/fragments, null storms, a past-50,000-row volume attack that must fail by design rather than by LimitException, and a user-mode authority attack run as a user without field access.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Winter '27 / API 68.0 is the current line and the guide's 67.0 fork is placed correctly; the sf CLI remains on its weekly v2 train, which the guide handles by naming the tool rather than a version.
toolchain_pins.evidence: All version-sensitive claims spot-checked (67.0 defaults, FIELDS() support, OFFSET ceiling) are current.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Execution surface and API version context declared per body of SOQL; sourceApiVersion/apiVersion pins reviewed when moved because behavior forks on version; sf CLI named for terminal execution; embedded apex_ls completion named instead of a fictitious standalone server.

current_versions.apex_ls: SOQL completion remains embedded in the Jorje Apex Language Server; no standalone SOQL language server, formatter or debugger exists - as the guide states
current_versions.code_analyzer: v5 PMD Apex rules are the static-analysis surface for queries inside Apex; the Query Plan tool remains the selectivity oracle
current_versions.salesforce_platform: Winter '27, API 68.0; the version-sensitive line the guide draws at API 67.0 (user-mode and with-sharing defaults) is the Summer '26 fork and is stated correctly
current_versions.sf_cli: sf CLI v2, weekly train (2.153.6 at 2026-09-30); sf data query / --bulk are the guide's execution surfaces, unchanged

proposals.evidence: Salesforce's Winter '27 developer coverage lists FORMULA() in SOQL as a Beta, sandbox-only capability - not production best practice today, so the guide is right to omit it now.
proposals.proposal: Watch the Winter '27 Beta FORMULA() function in SOQL WHERE clauses (API 68.0+, sandbox/Developer Edition/scratch orgs only at announcement): if it reaches GA, add a selectivity rule for formula-in-filter queries alongside the existing non-deterministic-formula warning.
proposals.recommendation: Watch only - do not document Beta syntax as a production rule.
